'''Douglas James Scalapino''' (born December 10, 1933, San Francisco, California)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://history.aip.org/history/ead/eaccpf/11609006.html|title=Scalapino, Douglas J. - Scientific Biographies|work=aip.org|accessdate=11 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170308133529/http://history.aip.org/history/ead/eaccpf/11609006.html|archive-date=8 March 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> is an [[Americans|American]] [[physicist]] noted for his contribution to [[theoretical condensed matter physics]].

== Career ==
Scalapino completed his [[undergraduate degree]] at [[Yale]] in 1955, and his PhD at [[Stanford]] in 1961.<ref name="ucsb.edu">{{cite web|url=http://web.physics.ucsb.edu/~djs/|title=Douglas Scalapino|work=ucsb.edu|accessdate=11 March 2017}}</ref> He then followed [[Edwin Thompson Jaynes|Ed Jaynes]] to become a research associate at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] from 1961 to 1962 and then moved to University of Pennsylvania where he attained the rank of full professor in 1969.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11609006.html|title=Scalapino, Douglas J.|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2019-12-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://web.physics.ucsb.edu/~djs/docs/cv.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae|last=Scalapino|first=Douglas|date=|website=UCSB Physics Department|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191229004025/http://web.physics.ucsb.edu/~djs/docs/cv.pdf |archive-date=2019-12-29 |access-date=}}</ref> He is currently a [[Research Professor]] of [[Physics]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref name="ucsb.edu"/>

In 1991 he became a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and in 1992 he became a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. In 1998, he received the [[Julius Edgar Lilienfeld Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Douglas&last_nm=Scalapino&year=1998|title=Prize Recipient|work=aps.org|accessdate=11 March 2017}}</ref> In 2013, he and [[Patrick A. Lee|Patrick Lee]] received the [[:de:Feenberg-Medaille|Eugene Feenberg Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.news.ucsb.edu/2013/013574/uc-santa-barbara-physics-professor-receive-eugene-feenberg-medal|title=UC Santa Barbara Physics Professor to Receive Eugene Feenberg Medal|website=The UCSB Current|date=3 July 2013 |language=en|access-date=2019-12-29}}</ref>
